newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor details Evander Gold Mines merger.
newsitem.headline: Gencor details Evander Gold Mines merger.

text.p: Gencor Ltd said on Monday that its Kinross Mines Ltd would acquire the mining operations of Winkelhaak Mines Ltd, Leslie Gold Mines Ltd and Bracken Mines Ltd.
Kinross would change its name to Evander Gold Mines (EGM).
The transaction would take effect from July 1, 1996 and Kinross would acquire the mining companies and their assets and liabilities in exchange for an aggregate of 11.8 million EGM shares.
Thereafter the EGM shares would be distributed to the shareholders of Winkelhaak, Leslie and Bracken by means of capital reductions.
Winkelhaak, Leslie and Bracken would then be delisted.

Kinross would also acquire from Gencor 14,107 hectares of virgin mineral rights and 1,186 hectares of mineral rights subject to lease agreements. The aggregate consideration for thee mineral rights will be 5.7 EGM shares.
EGM will be listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) and on the London Stock Exchange (LSE) with effect from November 18.
Gencor said that once the merger was approved by shareholders of all four mining companies, the consulting services agreement held by Gencor in respect of Winkelhaak and Leslie would be terminated.
The Kinross consulting agreement would be cancelled in exchange for 127.6 million rand cash and Gencor would be obliged to use this cash to subscribe for 2.8 million EGM shares.

Gencor will be obliged to extend a renounceable claw-back offer to those Kinross, Winkelhaak, Bracken and Leslie shareholders registered on November 15 at a price of 4,544 cents per EGM share in respect of any EGM shares acquired via the cancellation.

Subject to the cancellation of the Kinross consulting services agreement, Gencor will offer for subscription by way of a renounceable rights to the claw-back offerees and/or their renouncees, a total of about 1.9 million EGM shares at a price of 4,544 cents per EGM share in the following ratios:
